extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, and journalism students interested in narrative/longform reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and best practices for selecting, reporting, and constructing longform narrative journalism pieces that emphasize scene, character, and meaning rather than breaking-news immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-by-scene construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scene-by-scene construction rather than abstract summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build the story through concrete scenes that show action and interaction instead of summarizing events; central to Tom Wolfe's New Journalism techniques and to 'show, don't tell' narrative reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Record dialogue as spoken to reflect realistic speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture spoken language accurately (verbatim when possible) to convey character and immediacy; dialogue should feel authentic and advance the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view of specific characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story from the point of view of specific characters rather than an omniscient abstract narrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a character-centered POV to ground readers in lived experience and make meaning through individual perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include everyday details that reveal social reality and status relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use telling ordinary details (clothing, possessions, settings, rituals) to illuminate class, power, and social dynamics; these small details help readers infer broader context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (Three-Aspect Structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the context behind the story: time, place, background conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the world in which events occur so readers understand stakes and norms before complications unfold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complication (Three-Aspect Structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the main events or disruptive series of events that drive the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the central conflict or series of incidents that create momentum and require response from characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome (Three-Aspect Structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the aftermath or consequences of the complication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude with what changes, what remains unresolved, and the human consequences — outcomes may be ambiguous rather than neatly closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should contain enough complexity to leave readers in uncomfortable places and produce emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer subjects with layered contradictions, moral ambiguity, or tangled motives that resist easy summary and provoke reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling main character
rubrics_metrics.description: A central, compelling character who can guide the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find a person whose choices, emotions, or perspective can carry the reader through the story and reveal larger truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-layered access
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources willing to share across weeks or months and provide depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longform requires sustained access — multiple sources who will open up over time and permit deep reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying universal theme
rubrics_metrics.description: A theme that goes beyond the facts to touch universal concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a thematic frame that connects the specific narrative to broader human or social questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-rich subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects that are not breaking news and that reward extended time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose topics that unfold over longer periods or benefit from long observation rather than immediate events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual scene potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that offer vivid, describable scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the subject yields concrete, cinematic moments that can be rendered on the page for reader immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible to follow over time
rubrics_metrics.description: A story that can be tracked longitudinally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure there are developments or evolutions to be observed so the narrative can sustain reader interest across many paragraphs or pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that connects emotionally with readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize situations that evoke empathy, surprise, outrage, or other strong reactions; resonance often outweighs immediacy in longform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be something that matters — consequences, risks, or moral weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify what is at stake for characters or communities to give the narrative purpose and urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should be original and not previously well-covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek fresh angles, overlooked subjects, or new reporting that adds materially to public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources explored in depth (Reporting Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use numerous, deeply explored sources to substantiate the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate and corroborate information across many interviews and documents rather than relying on a few statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weeks or months of reporting (Reporting Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to spend extended time researching and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longform typically requires prolonged engagement — weeks or months — to develop nuance and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous fact-checking (Reporting Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply stringent fact-checking processes to all claims and details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triple-check facts where possible; fact-checking is explicitly listed among best practices for longform reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning to subjects multiple times (Reporting Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisit sources repeatedly rather than relying on single interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent contact allows verification, observation of change, richer quotes, and deeper trust-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living with subjects when possible (Reporting Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spend immersive time near or among subjects when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immersion reporting (e.g., living with subjects) can reveal routine details and dynamics not accessible in short interviews; ethical considerations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance over recency (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize emotional and thematic resonance rather than freshness of event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longform values depth and lasting insight more than being first to report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character over event (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let people drive the story rather than treating it as an isolated incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characters to explore consequences, motives, and the human dimension of larger issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene over summary (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor vivid scenes that show action instead of summarizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenes make abstract issues tangible and keep readers immersed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity over closure (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept uncomfortable or unresolved endings rather than forcing neat conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longform can leave ambiguity to reflect real-world complexity; endings can be evocative rather than fully resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern over incident (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize patterns, systems, or what the story illuminates beyond a single incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an individual case to reveal broader social, institutional, or cultural patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underdog stories (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories about overlooked or marginalized subjects are valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek narratives that give voice to people or communities typically ignored by mainstream coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden communities (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose worlds readers are unfamiliar with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthropological curiosity and access to closed or overlooked groups can yield powerful longform material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process / ritual (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how things actually work — routines, rituals, and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed depiction of process can illuminate institutions and everyday practice for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity / belonging themes (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore questions of identity and belonging as central story threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that probe belonging, identity transitions, or cultural affiliation often resonate deeply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lives in transition (Implicit Newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on people undergoing change or transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional periods reveal character and conflict and naturally structure narrative arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the right story (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select stories with both resonance and access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance emotional/thematic weight with practical ability to report (access to sources, time, and scenes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop multiple sources (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a network of sources rather than relying on a single informant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple corroborating perspectives strengthen accuracy and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spend significant time (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicate substantial time to reporting and immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longform requires patience and sustained observation to capture nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build trust slowly (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earn subjects' confidence over time before expecting full access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust-building enables candid interviews, better access, and ethical reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take rigorous notes (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record detailed notes during reporting to preserve accuracy and detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes support reconstruction of scenes, dialogue, and chronological order; they aid fact-checking and drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scene-by-scene construction (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the story in sequential scenes to maintain narrative momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenes should be crafted to reveal character, conflict, and theme progressively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture dialogue accurately (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure quoted speech reflects what was actually said when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate dialogue enhances realism and credibility; attribute paraphrase when verbatim is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a character who can carry the story (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a protagonist whose arc will engage readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong central character provides emotional focus and narrative continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a thematic frame (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a thematic lens that organizes facts and scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear theme helps readers understand why the story matters and ties scenes together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan structure carefully (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the narrative architecture before or during drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think through openings, turning points, pacing, and how scenes build toward an ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test multiple drafts (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise repeatedly and experiment with structure and emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing drafts — including sequencing and framing — helps clarify focus and strengthen storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong opening (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with an engaging, vivid opening that draws readers in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An evocative lead sets tone, establishes stakes, and signals what the story will explore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build to memorable ending (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft an ending that leaves a lasting impression, even if ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endings can synthesize theme, reveal consequence, or leave provocative questions rather than providing tidy closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple fact-check (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply multiple layers of fact-checking to verify all material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-checking should be exhaustive for names, dates, quotes, and factual assertions; the guideline explicitly recommends triple-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit ruthlessly (Best Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be ruthless in editing to sharpen prose, structure, and focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut extraneous detail, tighten scenes, and ensure each element serves theme, character, or plot progression.
